facts.fact: Punch reports the NDPC, with National Commissioner and CEO Vincent Olatunji and Head of Legal, Enforcement and Regulations Babatunde Bamigboye, issued a statement on Tuesday 28 July 2026 directing unregistered Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance to register.

In Emmanuel Harunna v. NDPC (FHC/L/CS/1116/2024) Justice F.N. Ogazi examined sections 5(d), 6(c), 44, 45 and 65 of the Act and the NDPC cites Section 63 as prevailing over inconsistent law; the article gives no judgment date and is dated 28 July 2026.

The court concluded the NDPC acted within its statutory powers in its Guidance Notice on Registration designating entities in the Major Data Processing - Ordinary High Level category as Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance; no issue date is given and the article is dated 28 July 2026.

A Federal High Court judgment affirmed the NDPC's power to designate and register Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance against a challenge on behalf of PoS agents; the judgment date is not given and the article is dated 28 July 2026.
After the judgment the NDPC issued a fresh directive on 28 July 2026 that every unregistered Data Controller and Processor of Major Importance register without delay, warning of legal consequences.

note: Sweep note in the file flags that Section 63 versus 65 for the supremacy clause is unresolved between accounts; recorded as stated here.
